//: DRAFT: every feel number in the game lives in this one file, so the owner can change how it plays without touching code. Units: pixels (at the 320x180 scale) and seconds. Each number is declared, with its allowed range, by the verb or system that reads it (src/sim/verbs/, src/sim/systems/); npm run check names any number that is missing, out of range or unread.

world.//: DRAFT (Step 4, people): how far a person sees, how much oddness makes rage, how long distress and rage last, how near a hero must be to use a thing. Every one is a first guess. DRAFT (Step 4, the town's tiers; docs/decisions-log.md, "Step 4: whistle"): npcWhistleTime and npcWhistleAgain, how long a guard on duty blows his whistle and how long he waits before he may blow again; npcDispatchCapOn is a control switch for scenarios only.

DRAFT (Step 23, weapons; decisions-log "Step 23"): weaponPickupReach, how far past its box a hero still touches a loose weapon to pick it up with Use. weaponStaysWithHero (the owner, 2026-11-24: one weapon per hero, not per party): 1, a weapon stays with the party member who picked it up through a switch; 0, it follows the player. weaponBurstShow (push 4): seconds a burst bomb shows its burst look where it burst before it is gone.

shopkeeper.//: DRAFT (Step 4): people walk; they do not run or jump. INTENT (Step 18, there is always a way out): no jump, and slower than every hero runs; a person who runs or jumps needs another way out first. DRAFT (Step 18): attack numbers, an ordinary fighter (docs/plan/step-18.md).

toll-keeper.//: DRAFT (Step 18): the shopkeeper's walking numbers, copied when her set gained attack numbers; the toll keeper does not swing (content/characters/toll-keeper.json). INTENT (Step 18, there is always a way out): no jump, and slower than every hero runs; a person who runs or jumps needs another way out first.

guard.//: INTENT (Step 18, there is always a way out): no jump, and slower than every hero runs; a person who runs or jumps needs another way out first. DRAFT (Step 18): attack numbers, a camp fighter with a slower wind-up (docs/plan/step-18.md).

armoured-guard.//: DRAFT (Step 4, the town's tiers, push 3): the town's tougher guard, in the street's top row. INTENT (there is always a way out): no jump and slower than the guard (32 px/s against 40; every hero runs 76 or more). Weight 80, twice a guard's: a punch moves him about half as far. Toughness 180 (a guard's is 100): the grappler (34 wear) drops him in 6 punches, the skirmisher (14) in 13. A slower, harder swing.

villain.//: INTENT (Step 18, there is always a way out): no jump, and slower than every hero runs; a person who runs or jumps needs another way out first. DRAFT (Step 18): the guard's attack numbers, a melee swing once struck (docs/plan/step-18.md).

grappler.//: DRAFT: heavy: slower to start and stop, a little slower at full run. Feel (2026-11-23): falls hardest (fallGravity 1.5, fallSpeed 420), the longest wind-up (0.1 s); its ground start and stop are unchanged because other steps' scenarios walk it to doors to the tick.

infiltrator.//: DRAFT: quick and twitchy, with a lower jump. Feel (2026-11-23): full speed and a stop in 3 ticks, a small hang at the top, the lightest (weight 26), a two-frame wind-up.

flyer.//: DRAFT: light: a weak jump from the ground, good steering in the air. Feel (2026-11-23): floats (apexGravity 0.45, fallGravity 0.6, fallSpeed 170).

king.//: DRAFT (Step 6): as the heavy dummy: anyone can hit him, only the grappler lifts him.

outpost-fighter.//: DRAFT (Step 12): a camp fighter. Walks like a guard (a little quicker), swings like a lighter grappler.

outpost-lookout.//: DRAFT (Step 12): the camp lookout, quick on its feet so the run to the horn is a race.

signal-post.//: DRAFT (Step 12): the post with the horn. Like the throne: nobody can lift it and it cannot be knocked out. Heaviest a body may be, so a hit or a body knocked into it barely moves it.

pedestal.//: DRAFT (Step 7): as heavy as the heavy dummy, so only the grappler lifts it; it cannot be knocked out.

throne.//: DRAFT (Step 6): heavier than anyone can lift; it cannot be knocked out.

brawler.//: DRAFT (Step 11): the heavy brawler: slow, the hardest punch and the longest wind-up, hard to knock out. First guesses beside the grappler's.

skirmisher.//: DRAFT (Step 11): light and quick: fast on its feet, quick jabs that barely push, easy to send flying. First guesses beside the infiltrator's.

heavy-fighter.//: DRAFT (Step 16 slice 2): a heavy bad guy. Weight 120, three times a fighter's (world default 40): the grappler's punch launches it at about 117 px/s against a fighter's 350. Toughness 240: eight of the grappler's punches (34 wear each) drop it. A slam wears by speed (impactWear), and a grappler's throw of it only reaches about 217 px/s, so a throw wears less than a punch: no throw drops it alone (docs/decisions-log.md).

brute.//: DRAFT (Step 16 slice 2): a brute. Slow (28 px/s), a long wind-up, a hit that launches the grappler at 400 px/s and wears 45; weight 140 (only the grappler lifts it), toughness 480 (fifteen of the grappler's punches).

ram-wagon.//: DRAFT (Step 20): the ram wagon's body. Weight 200: a ram at 340 px/s sends a camp fighter (40) off at the launch cap and a heavy (120) at about 380; nobody on the roster can lift it (the grappler lifts 150); a body thrown into it barely moves it. Toughness 0: it is never knocked out, it wears to a wreck by its own count of crashes (content/machines/ram-wagon.json).

ranged-fighter.//: DRAFT (Step 24 slice 1): the thrower. Walks like the camp lookout (he never walks after a hero: systems/ranged-throw.ts), a weak swing up close (6000: a 40-weight body off at 150 px/s), the camp fighter's timings; weight 30 and toughness 50, light and fragile (D-021): two of the grappler's punches floor him.

forest-boulder.//: DRAFT (Step 15): heavier than every hero lifts (the grappler and the brawler lift 150) and than the heaviest hero with the heavy crate on a plate (the brawler 70 and the heavy crate 120: 190), under the boost's 420. Set down on the trail's heavy plate (needs 260) it holds the stone slab open. It cannot be knocked out.
